quests.question: By the time the plane landed, we had been flying ___ the storm for nearly an hour, unable to see the ground below.
quests.targetSentence: By the time the plane landed, we had been flying through the storm for nearly an hour, unable to see the ground below.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Through' fits movement inside something that surrounds you, like storm clouds; 'during' would only mark the timing, missing the sense of being enclosed in the weather.
quests.nativeTip: The plane is surrounded by weather on every side, not just passing over open ground.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'through' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'By the time the plane landed, we had been flying through the storm for nearly an hour, unable to see the ground below.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: by vs until
quests.question: We won't be able to check in ___ the hotel confirms availability, which could take until tomorrow.
quests.targetSentence: We won't be able to check in until the hotel confirms availability, which could take until tomorrow.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Until' shows the waiting continuing up to whenever confirmation arrives; 'by' would need a fixed deadline, which the sentence doesn't give.
quests.nativeTip: The waiting continues right up to an uncertain future moment, not a fixed deadline.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'until' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'We won't be able to check in until the hotel confirms availability, which could take until tomorrow.'

quests.question: She'd been staring ___ the map for ten minutes before finally spotting the right street.
quests.targetSentence: She'd been staring at the map for ten minutes before finally spotting the right street.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Stare at' follows the same pattern as 'look at', directing attention toward something visible.
quests.nativeTip: Her eyes are directed toward a specific object, the same pattern as looking at something.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'at' (Specific Point (e.g. at the door)) ➔ 'She'd been staring at the map for ten minutes before finally spotting the right street.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: tired of vs tired from
quests.question: He's not usually one to complain, but even he grew tired ___ the constant delays.
quests.targetSentence: He's not usually one to complain, but even he grew tired of the constant delays.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: tired of vs tired from
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Tired of' expresses being fed up with something emotionally; 'tired from' would instead suggest physical exhaustion caused by an effort.
quests.nativeTip: This is about patience running out, not physical exhaustion from an effort.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'of' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'He's not usually one to complain, but even he grew tired of the constant delays.'

quests.question: The company relies heavily ___ freelance contractors during peak season.
quests.targetSentence: The company relies heavily on freelance contractors during peak season.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Rely on' is the fixed combination for depending on someone or something.
quests.nativeTip: This links dependence to the thing being counted on.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'on' (Surface Contact (e.g. on the table)) ➔ 'The company relies heavily on freelance contractors during peak season.'

quests.question: Despite years of experience, she still gets nervous ___ public speaking engagements.
quests.targetSentence: Despite years of experience, she still gets nervous about public speaking engagements.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Nervous about' is the dominant modern form; 'nervous of' is an older, less common alternative.
quests.nativeTip: This is the standard modern form for describing anxiety toward an upcoming situation.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'about' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Despite years of experience, she still gets nervous about public speaking engagements.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: since vs for
quests.question: Although he'd only been working at the company ___ six months, he was already being considered for a promotion.
quests.targetSentence: Although he'd only been working at the company for six months, he was already being considered for a promotion.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'For' pairs with a stated duration, like six months, showing how long he had worked there.
quests.nativeTip: A length of time is stated here, not a starting event.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'for' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Although he'd only been working at the company for six months, he was already being considered for a promotion.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: by vs until
quests.question: The contract remains valid ___ either party chooses to terminate it in writing.
quests.targetSentence: The contract remains valid until either party chooses to terminate it in writing.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Until' shows a state continuing up to a future event that hasn't happened yet, here a possible termination.
quests.nativeTip: The contract stays in effect right up to an uncertain future action.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'until' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The contract remains valid until either party chooses to terminate it in writing.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: since vs for
quests.question: Ever ___ the merger was announced, employees have worried about layoffs.
quests.targetSentence: Ever since the merger was announced, employees have worried about layoffs.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Since' marks the starting point of an ongoing situation, here the worry beginning at the announcement.
quests.nativeTip: A specific past event marks the starting point of an ongoing feeling.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'since' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Ever since the merger was announced, employees have worried about layoffs.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: between vs among
quests.question: Tension had been building ___ the two rival departments for months before the merger finally forced them to collaborate.
quests.targetSentence: Tension had been building between the two rival departments for months before the merger finally forced them to collaborate.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Between' fits because exactly two departments are named, following the same rule taught for two people or things.
quests.nativeTip: Exactly two groups are named here.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'between' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Tension had been building between the two rival departments for months before the merger finally forced them to collaborate.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: above vs over
quests.question: The company's profits remained well ___ industry averages throughout the recession, a rare bright spot in an otherwise difficult year.
quests.targetSentence: The company's profits remained well above industry averages throughout the recession, a rare bright spot in an otherwise difficult year.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Above average' is the standard fixed comparison for performance figures; 'over average' isn't the natural idiom here.
quests.nativeTip: This is the standard fixed phrase for comparing performance to a general benchmark.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'above' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The company's profits remained well above industry averages throughout the recession, a rare bright spot in an otherwise difficult year.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: below vs under
quests.question: Morale sank even further ___ expectations once the layoff announcement was made.
quests.targetSentence: Morale sank even further below expectations once the layoff announcement was made.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Below expectations' is the standard fixed phrase for performance falling short of a benchmark, the same pattern as 'above average'.
quests.nativeTip: This is the standard fixed phrase for describing something falling short of a benchmark.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'below' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Morale sank even further below expectations once the layoff announcement was made.'

quests.question: The proposal was met ___ skepticism from several board members who doubted its feasibility.
quests.targetSentence: The proposal was met with skepticism from several board members who doubted its feasibility.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Met with' is the fixed idiom for describing the reaction something received, here skepticism.
quests.nativeTip: This links a reaction to the response it received.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'with' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The proposal was met with skepticism from several board members who doubted its feasibility.'

quests.question: Her promotion was largely attributed ___ her exceptional performance during the crisis.
quests.targetSentence: Her promotion was largely attributed to her exceptional performance during the crisis.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Attributed to' is the fixed idiom for crediting an outcome to a specific cause.
quests.nativeTip: This links an outcome back to its cause.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'to' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Her promotion was largely attributed to her exceptional performance during the crisis.'

quests.question: The new regulations will apply ___ all businesses operating within city limits, regardless of size.
quests.targetSentence: The new regulations will apply to all businesses operating within city limits, regardless of size.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Apply to' is the fixed idiom for describing who or what a rule affects.
quests.nativeTip: This links a rule to the group it affects.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'to' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The new regulations will apply to all businesses operating within city limits, regardless of size.'

quests.question: We'd been driving ___ the mountains for hours before we finally spotted a gas station.
quests.targetSentence: We'd been driving through the mountains for hours before we finally spotted a gas station.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Through' fits enclosed, surrounding terrain like mountains, following the same rule taught earlier with forests and tunnels.
quests.nativeTip: Mountains surround a road on every side, the same pattern taught with forests and tunnels.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'through' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'We'd been driving through the mountains for hours before we finally spotted a gas station.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: by vs until
quests.question: The negotiations dragged on ___ well past midnight, exhausting everyone in the room.
quests.targetSentence: The negotiations dragged on until well past midnight, exhausting everyone in the room.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Until' shows the negotiations continuing up to a late point in time, longer than expected.
quests.nativeTip: The talks kept going right up to a very late hour.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'until' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The negotiations dragged on until well past midnight, exhausting everyone in the room.'

quests.question: By the time the rescue team arrived, the hikers had drifted well ___ their planned route, adding several miles to the search area.
quests.targetSentence: By the time the rescue team arrived, the hikers had drifted well off their planned route, adding several miles to the search area.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Drifted off route' is a fixed idiom for straying away from an intended path without realizing it.
quests.nativeTip: This is the standard fixed phrase for straying away from an intended path.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'off' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'By the time the rescue team arrived, the hikers had drifted well off their planned route, adding several miles to the search area.'

quests.question: Her management style is remarkably similar ___ her predecessor's, which has made the transition smoother for the team.
quests.targetSentence: Her management style is remarkably similar to her predecessor's, which has made the transition smoother for the team.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Similar to' returns here, comparing two management styles as alike.
quests.nativeTip: This links two things being compared as alike, as taught earlier in this course.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'to' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Her management style is remarkably similar to her predecessor's, which has made the transition smoother for the team.'

quests.question: Despite their shared upbringing, the twins turned out to be completely different ___ each other in personality.
quests.targetSentence: Despite their shared upbringing, the twins turned out to be completely different from each other in personality.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Different from' remains the safest, most widely accepted form for contrasting two things in international English.
quests.nativeTip: This links two things being contrasted, the most widely accepted form across formal English.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'from' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Despite their shared upbringing, the twins turned out to be completely different from each other in personality.'

quests.question: He's always been particularly good ___ defusing tense situations at work, a skill that's earned him respect.
quests.targetSentence: He's always been particularly good at defusing tense situations at work, a skill that's earned him respect.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Good at' returns here, describing a specific professional skill.
quests.nativeTip: This links a skill to the specific activity it applies to, as taught earlier in this course.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'at' (Specific Point (e.g. at the door)) ➔ 'He's always been particularly good at defusing tense situations at work, a skill that's earned him respect.'

quests.question: Even though she'd applied ___ the position months earlier, she didn't hear back from the company until after the deadline had passed.
quests.targetSentence: Even though she'd applied for the position months earlier, she didn't hear back from the company until after the deadline had passed.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Applied for' fits because 'the position' is an opportunity, following the same rule taught earlier with scholarships.
quests.nativeTip: The object here is an opportunity, not an institution.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'for' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Even though she'd applied for the position months earlier, she didn't hear back from the company until after the deadline had passed.'

quests.question: The bridge, which was built ___ the early 1900s, has recently been restored to its original condition.
quests.targetSentence: The bridge, which was built in the early 1900s, has recently been restored to its original condition.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'In' is used for broad periods like decades and eras, the same rule that applies to months and years.
quests.nativeTip: A broad historical period, like a decade or era, takes the same word as a month or year.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'in' (Months & Periods (e.g. in July)) ➔ 'The bridge, which was built in the early 1900s, has recently been restored to its original condition.'

quests.question: Having worked ___ the same company for over a decade, she finally decided it was time for a change.
quests.targetSentence: Having worked at the same company for over a decade, she finally decided it was time for a change.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Worked at' treats the company as a specific workplace, a natural and common way to describe long-term employment.
quests.nativeTip: This treats the company as a specific workplace, not a role or activity.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'at' (Specific Point (e.g. at the door)) ➔ 'Having worked at the same company for over a decade, she finally decided it was time for a change.'

quests.question: The manager insisted ___ reviewing every report personally, despite having a capable team to delegate to.
quests.targetSentence: The manager insisted on reviewing every report personally, despite having a capable team to delegate to.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Insist on' returns here, showing firm determination to carry out a specific action.
quests.nativeTip: This links insistence to the specific action being pushed for, as taught earlier in this course.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'on' (Surface Contact (e.g. on the table)) ➔ 'The manager insisted on reviewing every report personally, despite having a capable team to delegate to.'

quests.question: Sales figures have fluctuated significantly ___ the last two quarters, reflecting an unpredictable market.
quests.targetSentence: Sales figures have fluctuated significantly over the last two quarters, reflecting an unpredictable market.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Over' is used for describing a trend or pattern across a recent period, such as the last two quarters.
quests.nativeTip: This describes a trend across a recent stretch of time, not a single starting point.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'over' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Sales figures have fluctuated significantly over the last two quarters, reflecting an unpredictable market.'

quests.spatialHierarchy: Enclosed Space / Volume (e.g. in the room)
quests.question: The two proposals differ ___ several key respects, especially regarding budget and timeline.
quests.targetSentence: The two proposals differ in several key respects, especially regarding budget and timeline.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Differ in' is the fixed idiom for the verb form of contrasting two things, distinct from the adjective phrase 'different from'.
quests.nativeTip: This is the fixed idiom for the verb form of describing a contrast, distinct from the adjective form taught earlier.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'in' (Enclosed Space / Volume (e.g. in the room)) ➔ 'The two proposals differ in several key respects, especially regarding budget and timeline.'

quests.question: Having been notified ___ the change in policy only an hour before the meeting, the staff had little time to prepare their objections.
quests.targetSentence: Having been notified of the change in policy only an hour before the meeting, the staff had little time to prepare their objections.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Notified of' is the standard formal idiom used in professional and legal contexts for informing someone of something.
quests.nativeTip: This is the standard formal form used in professional and legal communication.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'of' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Having been notified of the change in policy only an hour before the meeting, the staff had little time to prepare their objections.'

quests.question: The success of the campaign depended ___ factors that were, frankly, beyond anyone's control.
quests.targetSentence: The success of the campaign depended on factors that were, frankly, beyond anyone's control.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Depend on' returns here one final time, linking an outcome to the conditions that determine it.
quests.nativeTip: This links an outcome to the conditions it relies on, as taught throughout this course.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'on' (Surface Contact (e.g. on the table)) ➔ 'The success of the campaign depended on factors that were, frankly, beyond anyone's control.'

quests.question: By the time she'd finished explaining the situation, everyone in the room understood exactly why she'd been so worried ___ the outcome.
quests.targetSentence: By the time she'd finished explaining the situation, everyone in the room understood exactly why she'd been so worried about the outcome.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Worried about' closes this unit, expressing anxiety toward an uncertain future result.
quests.nativeTip: This is general anxiety about a future result, the same pattern taught earlier in this course.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'about' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'By the time she'd finished explaining the situation, everyone in the room understood exactly why she'd been so worried about the outcome.'
